goals.notes: I believe in the AI revolution. I am a novice trader with not much history of success. I’d rather trade on high conviction stocks with strong growth outlooks, with some calibrated risks on stocks that could balloon, that tie into my belief in AI. I would rather not sink additional capital in if I don’t have to. I am okay to rebalance my portfolio to align with my goals. I can add capital if needed, but am already down 2 grand in loses this year. Don’t be afraid to make bold calls based on research and technicals that could find us a diamond in the rough type stock that explodes. WhileI believe in AI, putting all my chips in one basket has not been productive so I need a high growth mix.

thesis: Own a concentrated core of AI compute, data-center power and one great healthcare compounder, bought on weakness and held for years, funded by cutting the sub-2% tail positions rather than adding new cash, with a capped speculative sleeve for the asymmetric shot.
short_term: Hold VRT through Wednesday's earnings — do not sell the drop.
Sell all $155 of GEV and all $149 of ANET at market.
Sell all $192 of PANW at market to free up cash.
Buy $400 of LLY at market using those proceeds.
Keep AVGO — the plan says trim, I'd revise: it's a top AI pick.
Buy $475 of NU near $14.62 only once NVDA is back to break-even.
long_term: Core to hold for years: NVDA, AVGO, VRT, GOOGL, MSFT — add on weakness, never sell on price.
LLY is your second engine: 2026 guidance raised to $82-85B and a newly approved weight-loss pill.
Shrink from 15 positions to 8-10 so your best ideas actually move the account.
Keep the power sleeve near 12% through CEG, down 20% this year while signing data-center contracts.
Add Financials — a theme you don't own — only via NU near $14.62, for its fast-growing digital bank.
Hold winners past one year; this year's booked losses offset gains you do take.
guardrails: No single position above 18% of the book; top five stay under 60%.
Speculative sleeve capped at 8% total, each pick near 3%, never averaged down.
Every speculative buy gets a stop set before entry — SMCI stop $21.
Core names are sold only on broken business news, never on a falling price.
If the book drops below $8,200, pause all new buying for two weeks.
milestones: By Sept 30 2026: book above $11,000 and trimmed to 11 positions or fewer.
By Dec 31 2026: book above $13,500 with healthcare at least 12%.
By July 2027: book above $16,000 — roughly halfway to the $25,000 goal.
By July 2029: $25,000 needs about 37% a year — treat it as a stretch, not a promise.
Check VRT and LLY each quarter: growth slowing two quarters running triggers a re-examination.
